AARON ALDERMAN / dad

An idea becomes a path.

Follow small practices of attention, patience and care: the work of making room for a child and returning after a difficult moment.

← dad / HomeThreadsMapQuestions

Be here before solving it

Notice the person in front of the problem.

  1. The same clearing. A different field of attention.

    Looking closely at one thing can make its surroundings harder to notice.

  2. What are they trying to do?

    Before answering, ask what the other person is trying to do.

  3. Remember to care.

    Who or what needs my attention here?

Make room to grow

Care includes boundaries and room for another will.

  1. Leaving room is still a choice.

    Holding back can give someone room. It can also leave someone exposed.

  2. What changes when time is short?

    Waiting has different costs when needs are more urgent.

  3. An intention is not yet an action.

    Choosing to act and carrying out an action are different parts of a story.

Return after getting it wrong

Stay available for revision and another beginning.

  1. Let the correction leave a seam.

    When an explanation changes, leave a way to understand why.

  2. Back where you started. Something has changed.

    You can come back to the same place with something facing a different way.

  3. Remember to care.

    Who or what needs my attention here?
